item.title: Protests update at Bord Bia HQ
item.description: The chairperson of the Cavan IFA says that ongoing protest at the Bord Bia buildings in Dublin is still going strong as no resolution has been reached yet. The protest has been taking place for 11 days, and has continued with protestors entering the building. The IFA is protesting against Bord Bia chairperson Larry Murrin, after it emerged that his company, Dawn Farms' imported Brazilian beef. item.title: Man further remanded in jail over Cavan/Monaghan thefts
item.description: A 33-year-old man has been further remanded in custody in relation to a spate of thefts from businesses across Cavan, Louth, Meath and Monaghan. Luke Wall, with an address at Cois na hAbhann, Bonninconlon, Ballina, Co Mayo, appeared before Monaghan District Court. Judge Raymond Finnegan at Monaghan District Court was told that a book of evidence is awaited in this case. item.title: Local calls to 'streamline' Garda vetting process
item.description: A Monaghan Aontú rep is calling for the Garda vetting process for volunteers to be "more efficient" in order to free up Garda time. Olivia Larkin highlighted the importance of Garda setting and safeguarding when it comes to ensuring the protection of young, elderly and vulnerable people. item.title: Focus on Hurling as football takes a break
item.description: The focus this weekend will be on hurling with the National football league taking a break. On Saturday Monaghan will be looking to make it back to back wins in Division 4 when they host Longford in Paric Gratten Inniskeen at 2pm. Following an opening day loss to promotion favourites Sligo, the Farney side picked up their first points in round 2 with a 1-23 to 2-16 victory over Lancashire. item.description: In the Lidl Ladies league Division 2, both Cavan and Monaghan have home advantage in round 3 this weekend. Monaghan who are still in search of their first points host Westmeath at St Marys Park in Castleblayney on Sunday at 2pm . The visitors are in a similiar position following defeats to Donegal and Tyrone. item.title: Monaghan duo to appear in court over Shannon airport protest
item.description: Activists from Co. Monaghan are set to appear before the courts in Ennis, Co. Clare next week. Áine Ní Thréinir and Aindriú de Buitléir from Monaghan and Eimear Walshe from Longford, will go on trial for an action at Shannon Airport. They are accused of gaining access to the runway area at Shannon Airport in March 2024 and attempting to disrupt the activities of two US military planes before being arrested by Gardaí. item.title: Major traffic incident being reported in Dublin city centre
item.description: Gardaí and the emergency services are at the scene of a major traffic incident in Dublin city centre. RTE News are reporting that a number of people have been seriously injured. A Bus Éireann double decker bus was coming up Talbot street at around 12.30pm to take a left on to the one way system on to Marlborough Street. item.title: Farmers hold Bord Bia protest in Monaghan Town
item.description: The Irish Farmers' Association hosted a protest outside the Hilgrove Hotel in Monaghan Town this morning. There was a Bord Bia meeting in Monaghan this morning, to discuss future standards for the organisation. Local IFA members felt that the protest was "irresponsible", given that protests against Larry Murrin are continuing in Dublin. item.title: Young Cavan entrepreneur tells his story
item.description: A young Cavan farmer has spoken about the business he has started operating, relating to egg vending machines. Ben Tierney grew up on a free-range hen farm, and says he has been gathering eggs for as long as he can remember. After he finished school, he went on to Ballyhaise Agricultural College and says he had a definite interest in business. item.title: County Monaghan businesses invited to enter awards
item.description: Businesses across County Monaghan are being invited to enter Monaghan Business & Tourism Awards 2026. Monaghan County Council, in partnership with The Anglo-Celt, has launched the new initiative to celebrate excellence, innovation and enterprise. The awards were officially launched recently at the Nuremore Estate by McGettigans in Carrickmacross and will culminate in a gala awards ceremony on Thursday 17th April 2026.
